note:
ISO 2026-W33 runs from August 10 through August 16. Mars and Ceres are separated by about 0.1° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Uranus is about 4.5° in ecliptic longitude from Aldebaran in Taurus.

**Naked eye:** 🌑 New Moon — 17:36:45 UTC. The dark Moon favors faint targets and extended star fields. Use Kaus Australis, α Tel, Vega as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -7.5; direct motion; 10.5% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Solar conjunction in ecliptic longitude Aug 12 17:36 UTC. Conjunction with Mercury in ecliptic longitude Aug 11 13:41 UTC. Conjunction with Venus in ecliptic longitude Aug 16 07:10 UTC. Conjunction with Jupiter in ecliptic longitude Aug 12 00:01 UTC. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude -0.8; direct motion; 67.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Aug 11 13:41 UTC. Conjunction with Jupiter in ecliptic longitude Aug 15 11:22 UTC. Venus: Naked eye; magnitude -4.4; direct motion; 51.5% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Aug 16 07:10 UTC. Mars: Naked eye; magnitude 1.3; direct motion; 93.1% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 9.0; direct motion; 98.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: In solar glare; magnitude -1.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Aug 12 00:01 UTC. Conjunction with Mercury in ecliptic longitude Aug 15 11:22 UTC. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 0.6; retrograde motion; 99.8% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.7; direct motion; 99.9% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.7; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.5; retrograde motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** Trace the charted figure of Sct, then identify α Sct at its plotted position.

**Small telescope:** Eagle Nebula: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M18: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Omega Nebula: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M28: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Collinder 380: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M69: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M25: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; Sagittarius Cluster: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; M70: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance
